A test that counts a resource on the wrong side of a race is a real defect, not noise.

⚠️ ⛔ Do **not** read a green re-run as 「fixed」 — per the CI rule a re-run only ever confirms *which class* the failure is in. And ⛔ do not spend the re-run twice: the standing rule allows **one**.

⚠️ Line anchors rot — the card gives the case name (「reaps the whole session it started, holds no caller fd, and leaves nothing behind」); re-locate by that, ⛔ not by line number.

`Size/model suggestion:` S — but ⛔ not mechanical: deciding whether to wait on the resource or take the reading inside the child is a design call, so default judgement tier.

## Round returned `done` — the mechanism is named, and the card's hypothesis was wrong in both halves

`domain:spec` execution seat, 2026-09-16T21:08Z. PR **#18530**, head `65c97a07606986f3565a175afad63af12d53ec92`, 1 file +98/-18, `Clause-②: no`, `--pair 18530` exit 0.

### The mechanism, read from the tree rather than guessed

`sdui_spawn_detached` (`scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh:88`) **returns as soon as the pidfile is non-empty** (`:113-115`), and its runner writes that pid on its **first** line (`:96`) — before the for-fd loop that closes the descriptors inherited from the caller (`:98-105`), and before it execs. So the session leader the caller has just been told is ready is still a bash process **holding the caller's flock fd**.

Window measured over 25 runs with `EPOCHREALTIME` inside an instrumented copy: **151–297 µs**. The caller's margin (close minus count) is **10.4–54.3 ms**, and it is bought entirely by an unrelated `sleep 0.05` poll granularity at `:117`. A 0.2 ms critical section covered by a 50 ms sleep — which a six-way shard can invert, and did, once.

### Three premises falsified — two the card's, one the seat's

1. **"The count is taken after the child exits."** It is not. It is deliberately taken while the leader is alive (the comment at the old `:98-102`), and the failing job's own fields confirm it: `LEADER=4615 LEADER_SID=4615 LOCKFDS=1 LEADER_ALIVE_AT_COUNT=yes`.
2. **"An fd inherited by a grandchild."** Measured out: a node process holding an inherited non-cloexec fd reads `PARENT_SELF_LOCKFDS=1` while the child it spawns reads `HELPER_LOCKFDS=0` — libuv closes it across the spawn.
3. ⭐ **The seat's.** The dispatch **and** the claim both placed the cleanup path "under `packages/spec/scripts/`". It is at **repo-root `scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh`** — the test resolves `HERE` up three levels and into `scripts/`. **The clause as written authorised nothing**, and the round stopped at the fence rather than widening on a path the seat had mis-specified. That is the **second** file-surface drafting error this seat made today (the other is recorded on #18451); ⛔ neither is a dev overreach, and both are the seat's to fix in the claim template.

### The fix — ordering, not loosening

The stub takes the reading **of itself** after `exec` has replaced the closing shell, and publishes it; the harness waits for that **report** (never for a value), waits for the helper to join the session, then takes the same session-wide count and **names its holders**. The stub is released by a file instead of a 1200 ms timer, so `LEADER_ALIVE_AT_COUNT` stops racing node's boot, and the orphan precondition waits for `PPID 1` instead of sleeping two seconds. ⛔ Nothing was skipped, loosened to `toBeLessThan`, retry-wrapped or given a longer timeout — the one outcome this card must not have produced.

### Non-vacuity, proven in both directions

- **Ablation 1 — the lagging state.** A `sleep 0.5` injected between the pid publish and the fd-close loop of the **real** script (mutation proved on disk: marker 0→1, blob `5233551907…` → `ae6b02e6…`). Under that lag the **new** test passes; the **old** test, restored from base into the same worktree, **fails**: `LOCKFDS=2 / LEADER_ALIVE_AT_COUNT=yes / expected 2 to be 0`.
- **Ablation 2 — the new assertion's own teeth.** Disabling the fd hygiene (`if [ -d /proc/PID/fd ]` → `if false`) makes the new test **fail**, naming the holder: `LOCKFD_HOLDERS=[ 28876(node)]` — the exec'd leader, i.e. the process that can actually survive cleanup. Both barriers read `yes`, so the red is the property and not a barrier artefact.
- Restores proved by blob hash against HEAD on both legs, `RESTORE_DIFF_HEAD=[]`, under a trap; an empty hash would have exited 91 and a mismatch 92.
- ⭐ **The confounder the seat named was ruled out by measurement, not by argument.** Inside `os-verify-lock.sh` the probe reads `SESSION_VERIFYLOCK_FDS=0` / `CALLER_VERIFYLOCK_FDS=0`, with a **lit control** — a process deliberately holding `/tmp/os-heavy-verify.lock` reads `1`. So those zeros are facts, and the wrapper is not in the counted tree.

### Evidence

Subject test ×5 → exit 0 each, 1.71–2.91 s (base 4.47 s; the blind `sleep 2` is gone). `test:repo` — **the very project and shard that failed** — 31 files / 526 tests, exit 0. Full `packages/spec` test 482 passed / 1 skipped. Typecheck exit 0, and `check:test-typecheck` confirms the edited file is inside a `tsc` program. 58 derived gate families, all 58 run: 53 exit 0, **5 exit 3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET = NOT MEASURED** (each refuses for a missing built `dist/`), reconciled by `--ran` with 0 UNRUN. `skip-changeset` measured rather than assumed: `npm pack --dry-run --json` lists 271 entries, **0 under `scripts/`**, with README/llms.txt/package.json as the positive control.

### The open question, adjudicated: **A**

> Should `sdui_spawn_detached` also be reordered so the pidfile becomes a real readiness barrier?

**A — leave the script alone**, as this PR does. The round's own measurement carries the decision: the pre-exec shell has no path that skips the close, nothing in the script reads the leader's descriptors, and the only consumer that ever cared was this test's measurement point — which is now ordered on the resource. **B** would widen the existing "pid not yet recorded" window to cover the close loop, trading a real (if tiny) reapability hole for a contract nicety, and `sdui_stop_detached` returns 0 on an empty pidfile, so that hole is silent. **C** pays structural cost for the same nicety in a helper whose whole design note is that a cleanup which can fail silently is the defect.

⇒ ⛔ No card for B now. If a **second** consumer of that pidfile ever appears, B becomes a card against repo-root `scripts/` with its own reapability argument — ⛔ not a scope extension of this one. The discrepancy between `sdui_spawn_detached`'s doc comment ("no inherited descriptors above stderr") and what the pidfile actually promises is recorded here, in front of the next author, rather than buried.

### The other calls, affirmed

- **The old orphan scan** (a `for` loop whose body was a test-and-assign AND-list) leaned on `set -e`'s AND-list exemption and would have aborted the harness if a non-orphan member were ever scanned last; it only ever passed because the session holds exactly one member. Rewritten as an `if` in the same stroke and declared in the PR body — a bounded in-place fix of the same defect class (a blind construct standing in for a barrier), same file, same gate family, no new verification surface. ⛔ Not a widening.
- **The label write.** The round wrote `skip-changeset` on the PR (`POST /issues/18530/labels`, read back `['skip-changeset']`, nothing stripped) and disclosed it. It is not the review gate, it is part of this PR's own declaration shape, and it was measured before it was written. Accepted, and recorded because a dev label write is worth seeing rather than discovering.
- **One MCP call**, `mcp__github__get_job_logs` (a **read**), because the Actions log blob host answers 403 through the agent proxy. The rule is 0 MCP GitHub **writes**; the name is listed, as required.

CI on `65c97a0760` at 21:08:43Z: 11 success, 5 skipped, **16 in progress, 0 failure** — `Test Core (1/6)`, the shard this card is about, is still running and is **NOT MEASURED** until it concludes. ⚠️ That shard is precisely where this fix has to prove itself, so its verdict is the one that matters and the seat is watching it.

This PR declares `Clause-②: no`, so ⛔ it does not join the at-tier review backlog and can land on its own three conditions once the shard reports.

A PR that waits loses time; one landed without a review the rules wanted cannot be un-landed.
